title: Intelligence report from Port Sainte-Marie (Spain) in numerical code, enclosed to the Duke of Newcastle, undeciphered
correspondents: unnamed British agent at Port Sainte-Marie → Thomas Pelham-Holles, Duke of Newcastle (via a correspondent at 'Cesnok', signature illegible)
place: El Puerto de Santa María (Spain); covering letter from 'Cesnok'
shelfmark: Huntington Library, William Blathwayt papers addenda, mssBLA 191 (HDL p15150coll7 id 61008)
folio_note: 6 pp. + cover; enclosure (a) is one full page of about 140 three- and four-digit code groups (p. 5, HDL page 61005), no interlinear decipherment; enclosure (b) 21 July 1729 is in clear French
status: Catalogue: 'Enclosure: Two letters from Port Ste Marie: (a) undated, in cipher; (b) July 21, 1729, in French.' No decipherment noted. Image viewed 28 Oct 2026: p. 5 is pure code, unglossed. The same code (groups 659, 1013, 1250, 580, 26, 18 ...) is deciphered interlinearly on the enclosure of mssBLA 187 (letter of 23 June 1729, endorsed 'in the letter of 23 Juin 1729', deciphered 19 July 1729) and is noted as deciphered on mssBLA 188 and the 14 July and 4 Aug 1729 letters. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: A British spy's report from Andalusia in the summer of the Treaty of Seville negotiations (Spanish galleons, Gibraltar, Ripperdá era) that was never decoded on the leaf; the code book can be rebuilt from five deciphered sibling letters in the same file.
score_note: Scored from the archive description and the page image during the Oct 2026 Huntington Library sweep (research/us_huntington/)
verify: Transcribe the deciphered siblings mssBLA 187 (HDL 60966), 188 (HDL 60924), 14 July 1729 (HDL 60892) and 4 Aug 1729 (HDL 60914) into a code table, then apply it to HDL 61005.

title: Letter of intelligence from Madrid on Ripperdá's escape from Segovia, with one line in numerical code
correspondents: unnamed intelligence agent (Madrid) → unnamed British recipient (Blathwayt/Hume-Campbell intelligence file)
shelfmark: Huntington Library, William Blathwayt papers addenda, mssBLA 186 (HDL p15150coll7 id 61211)
folio_note: 4 pp. + note + cover; p. 1 has one coded run of 11 groups (659.78.73.18.438.468.470.778.190.1102.53) in an otherwise clear letter
status: Catalogue: 'In French, with two lines in cipher.' No decipherment noted; image viewed 28 Oct 2026, the coded run is unglossed. why: The coded line follows the news that the fallen minister Ripperdá had escaped from Segovia castle and the court's request to foreign ministers to hand him over; it likely names who helped him or where he went.
